spob.text: Then the city’s defenses were broken through. That night, all the fighting men fled through the gate between the two walls beside the king’s garden. Although the Chaldeans surrounded the city on every side, the king headed toward the Arabah.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Then the city was breached; and though the Chaldeans had surrounded the city, all the men of war fled by night by way of the gate between the two walls near the king’s garden. They headed toward the Arabah,
public_domain_references.web: Then a breach was made in the city, and all the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king’s garden (now the Chaldeans were against the city around it); and the king went by the way of the Arabah.
public_domain_references.asv: Then a breach was made in the city, and all the men of war [fled] by night by the way of the gate between the two walls, which was by the king’s garden (now the Chaldeans were against the city round about); and [the king] went by the way of the Arabah.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And the city was broken up, and all the men of war [fled] by night by the way of the gate between two walls, which [is] by the king’s garden: (now the Chaldees [were] against the city round about:) and [the king] went the way toward the plain.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the city was broken up, and all the men of war went forth by night, by the way of the gate between the walls, this is [the gate] of the king's garden: and the Chaldeans [were set] against the city round about: and [the king] went by the way of the plain.

pob.text: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho[b][a], and all his army was scattered from him.

spob.text: But the Chaldean army[a] chased the king and caught up with him on the plains of Jericho. All the king’s troops were scattered from him.

public_domain_references.bsb: but the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was separated from him.
public_domain_references.web: But the Chaldean army pursued the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
public_domain_references.asv: But the army of the Chaldeans pursued after the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the army of the Chaldees pursued after the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho: and all his army were scattered from him.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the force of the Chaldeans pursued the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho: and all his army was dispersed from about him.

pob.text: Then they captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah[a], and they pronounced judgment on him.

spob.text: They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah. There they passed sentence on him.

public_domain_references.bsb: The Chaldeans seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where they pronounced judgment on him.
public_domain_references.web: Then they captured the king and carried him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah; and they passed judgment on him.
public_domain_references.asv: Then they took the king, and carried him up unto the king of Babylon to Riblah; and they gave judgment upon him.
public_domain_references.kjv: So they took the king, and brought him up to the king of Babylon to Riblah; and they gave judgment upon him.
public_domain_references.brenton: And they took the king, and brought him to the king of Babylon to Reblatha; and he gave judgment upon him.

pob.text: They slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes[a], and he put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him with bronze fetters, and brought him to Babylon.

spob.text: They slaughtered Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes. Then he put out Zedekiah’s eyes[a], put him in bronze shackles, and brought him to Babylon.

public_domain_references.bsb: And they slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes. Then they put out his eyes, bound him with bronze shackles, and took him to Babylon.
public_domain_references.web: They killed Zedekiah’s sons before his eyes, then put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bound him in fetters, and carried him to Babylon.
public_domain_references.asv: And they slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him in fetters, and carried him to Babylon.
public_domain_references.kjv: And they slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he slew the sons of Sedekias before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Sedekias, and bound him in fetters, and brought him to Babylon.

pob.text: And in the fifth month[a], on the seventh day of the month—which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

spob.text: On the seventh day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of the reign of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, Nebuzaradan came to Jerusalem. He was the captain of the royal guard[a] and served the king of Babylon.

public_domain_references.bsb: On the seventh day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign over Babylon, Nebuzaradan captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, entered Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.web: Now in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.asv: Now in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, unto Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And in the fifth month, on the seventh [day] of the month, which [is] the nineteenth year of king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzar-adan, captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, unto Jerusalem:
public_domain_references.brenton: And in the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month (this [is] the nineteenth year of Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon), came Nabuzardan, captain of the guard, who stood before the king of Babylon, to Jerusalem.

pob.text: He burned the house of Yahweh[a], the king's house, all the houses of Jerusalem[b], and every great house with fire.

spob.text: He burned Yahweh’s house,[a] the king’s palace, every house in Jerusalem, and every house that was large or important.

public_domain_references.bsb: He burned down the house of the LORD, the royal palace, and all the houses of Jerusalem—every significant building.
public_domain_references.web: He burned Yahweh’s house, the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem. He burned every great house with fire.
public_domain_references.asv: And he burnt the house of Jehovah, and the king’s house; and all the houses of Jerusalem, even every great house, burnt he with fire.
public_domain_references.kjv: And he burnt the house of the LORD, and the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, and every great [man’s] house burnt he with fire.
public_domain_references.brenton: And he burnt the house of the Lord, and the king's house, and all the houses of Jerusalem, even every house did the captain of the guard burn.

pob.text: And all the army of the Chaldeans who were with the captain of the guard tore down the walls of Jerusalem all around[a].

spob.text: The entire Chaldean army that was with the captain of the guard tore down all the walls around Jerusalem.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: And the whole army of the Chaldeans under the captain of the guard broke down the walls around Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.web: All the army of the Chaldeans, who were with the captain of the guard, broke down the walls around Jerusalem.
public_domain_references.asv: And all the army of the Chaldeans, that were [with] the captain of the guard, brake down the walls of Jerusalem round about.
public_domain_references.kjv: And all the army of the Chaldees, that [were with] the captain of the guard, brake down the walls of Jerusalem round about.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the force of the Chaldeans pulled down the wall of Jerusalem round about.

pob.text: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried into exile the rest of the people who remained in the city[a], the deserters who had defected to the king of Babylon[c][b], and the rest of the multitude.

spob.text: Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, deported the remaining people in Jerusalem, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the population.

public_domain_references.bsb: Then Nebuzaradan captain of the guard carried into exile the people who remained in the city, along with the deserters who had defected to the king of Babylon and the rest of the population.
public_domain_references.web: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive the rest of the people who were left in the city and those who had deserted to the king of Babylon—all the rest of the multitude.
public_domain_references.asv: And the residue of the people that were left in the city, and those that fell away, that fell to the king of Babylon, and the residue of the multitude, did Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carry away captive.
public_domain_references.kjv: Now the rest of the people [that were] left in the city, and the fugitives that fell away to the king of Babylon, with the remnant of the multitude, did Nebuzar-adan the captain of the guard carry away.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Nabuzardan the captain of the guard removed the rest of the people that were left in the city, and the men who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude.

pob.text: But from the poorest of the land[b][a], the captain of the guard left some to be vinedressers and farmers.

spob.text: But the captain of the guard left behind some of the poorest people in the land to tend the vineyards and work the fields.

public_domain_references.bsb: But the captain of the guard left behind some of the poorest of the land to tend the vineyards and fields.
public_domain_references.web: But the captain of the guard left some of the poorest of the land to work the vineyards and fields.
public_domain_references.asv: But the captain of the guard left of the poorest of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen.
public_domain_references.kjv: But the captain of the guard left of the poor of the land [to be] vinedressers and husbandmen.
public_domain_references.brenton: But the captain of the guard left of the poor of the land to be vine-dressers and husbandmen.

pob.text: And the Chaldeans broke in pieces the bronze pillars that were in the house of Yahweh[a], and the stands, and the bronze sea that was in the house of Yahweh[b], and carried their bronze to Babylon.

spob.text: The Chaldean forces[a] broke apart the bronze pillars, the stands[b], and the large bronze basin called the Sea, all of which were in Yahweh’s temple. Then they carried the bronze from these objects to Babylon.

public_domain_references.bsb: Moreover, the Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars and stands and the bronze Sea in the house of the LORD, and they carried the bronze to Babylon.
public_domain_references.web: The Chaldeans broke up the pillars of bronze that were in Yahweh’s house and the bases and the bronze sea that were in Yahweh’s house, and carried the bronze pieces to Babylon.
public_domain_references.asv: And the pillars of brass that were in the house of Jehovah, and the bases and the brazen sea that were in the house of Jehovah, did the Chaldeans break in pieces, and carried the brass of them to Babylon.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the pillars of brass that [were] in the house of the LORD, and the bases, and the brasen sea that [was] in the house of the LORD, did the Chaldees break in pieces, and carried the brass of them to Babylon.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the Chaldeans broke to pieces the brazen pillars that were in the house of the Lord, and the bases, and the brazen sea that was in the house of the Lord, and carried their brass to Babylon.

pob.text: And the pots[a], the shovels, the snuffers, the dishes, and all the bronze vessels with which they ministered—they took away.

spob.text: They took away the pots, shovels, lamp trimmers,[a] dishes, and all the bronze utensils used in the temple service.

public_domain_references.bsb: They also took away the pots, shovels, wick trimmers, dishes, and all the articles of bronze used in the temple service.
public_domain_references.web: They took away the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the spoons, and all the vessels of bronze with which they ministered.
public_domain_references.asv: And the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass wherewith they ministered, took they away.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the pots, and the shovels, and the snuffers, and the spoons, and all the vessels of brass wherewith they ministered, took they away.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the caldrons, and the shovels, and the bowls, and the censers, and all the brazen vessels with which they minister, he took.

pob.text: And the firepans and the bowls—what was gold[d][c][b][a], and what was silver—the captain of the guard took.

spob.text: The captain of the guard also took the firepans[a] and bowls[b], both those made of gold and those made of silver.[c]

public_domain_references.bsb: The captain of the guard also took away the censers and sprinkling bowls—anything made of pure gold or fine silver.
public_domain_references.web: The captain of the guard took away the fire pans, the basins, that which was of gold, for gold, and that which was of silver, for silver.
public_domain_references.asv: And the firepans, and the basins, that which was of gold, in gold, and that which was of silver, in silver, the captain of the guard took away.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the firepans, and the bowls, [and] such things as [were] of gold, [in] gold, and of silver, [in] silver, the captain of the guard took away.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the captain of the guard took the fire-pans, and the gold and silver bowls.

pob.text: As for the two pillars[a], the one Sea, and the stands that Solomon had made for the house of Yahweh, there was no weighing the bronze of all these vessels.

spob.text: There was so much bronze in the two pillars, the large basin called the Sea, and the stands that Solomon had made for Yahweh’s temple that no one weighed all of it.

public_domain_references.bsb: As for the two pillars, the Sea, and the movable stands that Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the weight of the bronze from all these articles was beyond measure.
public_domain_references.web: The two pillars, the one sea, and the bases, which Solomon had made for Yahweh’s house, the bronze of all these vessels was not weighed.
public_domain_references.asv: The two pillars, the one sea, and the bases, which Solomon had made for the house of Jehovah, the brass of all these vessels was without weight.
public_domain_references.kjv: The two pillars, one sea, and the bases which Solomon had made for the house of the LORD; the brass of all these vessels was without weight.
public_domain_references.brenton: Two pillars, and one sea, and the bases which Solomon made for the house of the Lord: there was no weight of the brass of all the vessels.

pob.text: The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits[a], and a bronze capital was on it. The height of the capital was three cubits, with latticework and pomegranates all around on the capital, all of bronze. And the second pillar had the same[b], with the latticework.

spob.text: The first pillar was about 27 feet (8 meters) tall.[a] It had a bronze capital—a decorative top—about 4½ feet (1.4 meters) high. Bronze latticework and pomegranate-shaped ornaments went all around the capital. The second pillar had the same ornamentation, including the latticework.[b]

public_domain_references.bsb: Each pillar was eighteen cubits tall. The bronze capital atop one pillar was three cubits high, with a network of bronze pomegranates all around. The second pillar, with its network, was similar.
public_domain_references.web: The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and a capital of bronze was on it. The height of the capital was three cubits, with network and pomegranates on the capital around it, all of bronze; and the second pillar with its network was like these.
public_domain_references.asv: The height of the one pillar was eighteen cubits, and a capital of brass was upon it; and the height of the capital was three cubits, with network and pomegranates upon the capital round about, all of brass: and like unto these had the second pillar with network.
public_domain_references.kjv: The height of the one pillar [was] eighteen cubits, and the chapiter upon it [was] brass: and the height of the chapiter three cubits; and the wreathen work, and pomegranates upon the chapiter round about, all of brass: and like unto these had the second pillar with wreathen work.
public_domain_references.brenton: The height of one pillar [was] eighteen cubits, and the chapiter upon it was of brass: and the height of the chapiter was three cubits: the border, and the pomegranates on the chapiter round about were all of brass: and so it was with the second pillar with its border.

pob.text: The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest[a], Zephaniah the second priest[b], and the three keepers of the threshold.

spob.text: The captain of the guard took Seraiah, the chief priest, into custody, along with Zephaniah, the priest next in rank, and the three guards who watched the temple threshold.

public_domain_references.bsb: The captain of the guard also took away Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest of second rank, and the three doorkeepers.
public_domain_references.web: The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold;
public_domain_references.asv: And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold:
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And the captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, and Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door:
public_domain_references.brenton: And the captain of the guard took Saraias the high-priest, and Sophonias the second in order, and the three door-keepers.

pob.text: And from the city he took one official[a], who was appointed over the men of war, and five men from those who saw the king’s face, who were found in the city, and the scribe, the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land[c][b], and sixty men from the people of the land who were found in the city.

spob.text: From the city he took one official[a] who was in charge of the soldiers; five men who had direct access to the king[b] and were found there; the secretary to the army commander, who called up the people of the land for military service; and sixty men from the people of the land who were found in the city.

public_domain_references.bsb: Of those still in the city, he took a court official who had been appointed over the men of war, as well as five royal advisors. He also took the scribe of the captain of the army, who had enlisted the people of the land, and sixty men who were found in the city.
public_domain_references.web: and out of the city he took an officer who was set over the men of war; and five men of those who saw the king’s face, who were found in the city; and the scribe, the captain of the army, who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
public_domain_references.asv: and out of the city he took an officer that was set over the men of war; and five men of them that saw the king’s face, who were found in the city; and the scribe, the captain of the host, who mustered the people of the land; and threescore men of the people of the land, that were found in the city.
public_domain_references.kjv: And out of the city he took an officer that was set over the men of war, and five men of them that were in the king’s presence, which were found in the city, and the principal scribe of the host, which mustered the people of the land, and threescore men of the people of the land [that were] found in the city:
public_domain_references.brenton: And they took out of the city one eunuch who was commander of the men of war, and five men that saw the face of the king, that were found in the city, and the secretary of the commander-in-chief, who took account of the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land that were found in the city.

pob.text: Nebuzaradan[a], the captain of the guard[b], took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

spob.text: Nebuzaradan was commander of the guard. He took the men and brought them to the king of Babylon, who was at Riblah.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
public_domain_references.web: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah.
public_domain_references.asv: And Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah.
public_domain_references.kjv: And Nebuzar-adan captain of the guard took these, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah:
public_domain_references.brenton: And Nabuzardan the captain of the guard took them, and brought them to the king of Babylon to Reblatha.

pob.text: And the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath[b][a]. So Judah was taken into exile from its land.

spob.text: The king of Babylon struck them down and killed them at Riblah, in the territory of Hamath. So Judah was forced into exile, away from its land.

public_domain_references.bsb: There at Riblah in the land of Hamath, the king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death. So Judah was taken into exile, away from its own land.
public_domain_references.web: The king of Babylon attacked them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried away captive out of his land.
public_domain_references.asv: And the king of Babylon smote them, and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried away captive out of his land.
public_domain_references.kjv: And the king of Babylon smote them, and slew them at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah was carried away out of their land.
public_domain_references.brenton: And the king of Babylon smote them and slew them at Reblatha in the land of Æmath. So Juda was carried away from his land.

pob.text: As for the people who remained in the land of Judah[a], whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, he appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, over them.

spob.text: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left some of the people in the land of Judah. He put Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, in charge of them.

public_domain_references.bsb: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, over the people he had left behind in the land of Judah.
public_domain_references.web: As for the people who were left in the land of Judah whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, even over them he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor.
public_domain_references.asv: And as for the people that were left in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, even over them he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor.
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And [as for] the people that remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, even over them he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, ruler.
public_domain_references.brenton: And [as for] the people that were left in the land of Juda, whom Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon left, even over them he set Godolias son of Achicam son of Saphan.

pob.text: When all the commanders of the forces[a], they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and Johanan son of Kareah, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.

spob.text: When all the military commanders and their men heard that the king of Babylon had put Gedaliah in charge, they went to him at Mizpah. The commanders were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth from Netophah, and Jaazaniah son of a man from Maacah; their men went with them.

public_domain_references.bsb: When all the commanders of the armies and their men heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah as governor, they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah—Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, as well as their men.
public_domain_references.web: Now when all the captains of the forces, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor, they came to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, Johanan the son of Kareah, Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of the Maacathite, they and their men.
public_domain_references.asv: Now when all the captains of the forces, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor, they came to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan the son of Kareah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of the Maacathite, they and their men.
public_domain_references.kjv: And when all the captains of the armies, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor, there came to Gedaliah to Mizpah, even Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and Johanan the son of Careah, and Seraiah the son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah the son of a Maachathite, they and their men.
public_domain_references.brenton: And all the captains of the host, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had [thus] appointed Godolias, and they came to Godolias to Massephath, both Ismael the son of Nathanias, and Jona son of Careth, and Saraias, son of Thanamath the Netophathite, and Jezonias son of a Machathite, they and their men.

pob.text: Gedaliah swore to them and to their men[a], and said to them, “Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon[b], and it will go well for you.”

spob.text: Gedaliah gave his solemn promise to them and their men. He said, “Do not be afraid of the Babylonian officials.[a] Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon. Then things will go well for you.”

public_domain_references.bsb: And Gedaliah took an oath before them and their men, assuring them, “Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well with you.”
public_domain_references.web: Gedaliah swore to them and to their men, and said to them, “Don’t be afraid because of the servants of the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well with you.”
public_domain_references.asv: And Gedaliah sware to them and to their men, and said unto them, Fear not because of the servants of the Chaldeans: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you.
public_domain_references.kjv: And Gedaliah sware to them, and to their men, and said unto them, Fear not to be the servants of the Chaldees: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon; and it shall be well with you.
public_domain_references.brenton: And Godolias swore to them and their men, and said to them, Fear not the incursion of the Chaldeans; dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you.

pob.text: And it happened in the seventh month that Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the royal seed, came with ten men, and they struck down Gedaliah, and he died, along with the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.

spob.text: In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and grandson of Elishama came with ten men. Ishmael was a descendant of the royal line. They struck down Gedaliah, and he died. They also struck down the Judeans and the Chaldeans[a] who were with him at Mizpah.

public_domain_references.bsb: In the seventh month, however, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, who was a member of the royal family, came with ten men and struck down and killed Gedaliah, along with the Judeans and Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
public_domain_references.web: But in the seventh month, Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the royal offspring came, and ten men with him, and struck Gedaliah so that he died, with the Jews and the Chaldeans that were with him at Mizpah.
public_domain_references.asv: But it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, came, and ten men with him, and smote Gedaliah, so that he died, and the Jews and the Chaldeans that were with him at Mizpah.
public_domain_references.kjv: But it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, came, and ten men with him, and smote Gedaliah, that he died, and the Jews and the Chaldees that were with him at Mizpah.
public_domain_references.brenton: And it came to pass in the seventh month [that] Ismael son of Nathanias son of Helisama, of the seed royal, came, and ten men with him, and he smote Godolias, that he died, [him] and the Jews and the Chaldeans that were with him in Massepha.

pob.text: Then all the people[a], from the least to the greatest, and the commanders of the forces, arose and went to Egypt, because they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

spob.text: Then all the people, from the least important to the greatest, and the army commanders went to Egypt because they were afraid of the Chaldeans.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: Then all the people small and great, together with the commanders of the army, arose and fled to Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans.
public_domain_references.web: All the people, both small and great, and the captains of the forces arose and came to Egypt; for they were afraid of the Chaldeans.
public_domain_references.asv: And all the people, both small and great, and the captains of the forces, arose, and came to Egypt; for they were afraid of the Chaldeans.
public_domain_references.kjv: And all the people, both small and great, and the captains of the armies, arose, and came to Egypt: for they were afraid of the Chaldees.
public_domain_references.brenton: And all the people, great and small rose up, [they] and the captains of the forces, and went into Egypt; because they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

pob.text: And it happened in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah[a], in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year of his reign[c][b], lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of the prison.

spob.text: On the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, in the thirty-seventh year since King Jehoiachin of Judah was exiled, Evil-merodach king of Babylon lifted Jehoiachin’s head: he released him from prison and raised his status. This happened in the year of Evil-merodach’s reign.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: On the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month of the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Judah’s King Jehoiachin, in the year Evil-merodach became king of Babylon, he released King Jehoiachin of Judah from prison.
public_domain_references.web: In the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, Evilmerodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, released Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison,
public_domain_references.asv: And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the seven and twentieth day of the month, that Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year that he began to reign, did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison;
public_domain_references.kjv: ¶ And it came to pass in the seven and thirtieth year of the captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the seven and twentieth [day] of the month, [that] Evil-merodach king of Babylon in the year that he began to reign did lift up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah out of prison;
public_domain_references.brenton: And it came to pass in the thirty-seventh year of the carrying away of Joachim king of Juda, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, [that] Evialmarodec king of Babylon in the [first] year of his reign lifted up the head of Joachim king of Juda, and brought him out of his prison-house.

pob.text: He spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the thrones of the kings who were with him in Babylon[a][b].

spob.text: He spoke kindly to him. He gave him higher rank than the other kings with him in Babylon, placing his throne above theirs.

public_domain_references.bsb: And he spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and set his throne above the thrones of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
public_domain_references.web: and he spoke kindly to him and set his throne above the throne of the kings who were with him in Babylon,
public_domain_references.asv: and he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that were with him in Babylon,
public_domain_references.kjv: And he spake kindly to him, and set his throne above the throne of the kings that [were] with him in Babylon;
public_domain_references.brenton: And he spoke kindly to him, and set his throne above the thrones of the kings that were with him in Babylon;

pob.text: And he changed his prison clothes[a], and he ate bread continually before him all the days of his life.

spob.text: He changed out of his prison clothes. For the rest of his life, he regularly ate his meals in the king’s presence.[a]

public_domain_references.bsb: So Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes, and he dined regularly at the king’s table for the rest of his life.
public_domain_references.web: and changed his prison garments. Jehoiachin ate bread before him continually all the days of his life;
public_domain_references.asv: and changed his prison garments. And [Jehoiachin] did eat bread before him continually all the days of his life:
public_domain_references.kjv: And changed his prison garments: and he did eat bread continually before him all the days of his life.
public_domain_references.brenton: and changed his prison garments: and he ate bread continually before him all the days of his life.

pob.text: And his allowance[a], a continual allowance, was given to him from the king, the portion for each day on its day[b], all the days of his life.

spob.text: The king gave him a continuing allowance, supplying his allotted portion each day, for the rest of his life.

public_domain_references.bsb: And the king provided Jehoiachin a daily portion for the rest of his life.
public_domain_references.web: and for his allowance, there was a continual allowance given him from the king, every day a portion, all the days of his life.
public_domain_references.asv: and for his allowance, there was a continual allowance given him of the king, every day a portion, all the days of his life.
public_domain_references.kjv: And his allowance [was] a continual allowance given him of the king, a daily rate for every day, all the days of his life.
public_domain_references.brenton: And his portion, a continual portion, was given him out of the house of the king, a daily rate for every day all the days of his life.
